prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

S867: Ramp personnel shall be trained under the direction of the Ramp Control Lead to use the Ramp Movement Board without substituting system indications for required visual checks, radio coordination, and local safety procedures.
S868: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be trained to submit, review, and update Flight Intent Message data through approved interfaces and to assess the operational effect of Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time changes.
S869: Ground handling personnel shall be trained by the Ground Handling Dispatcher on the Handling Resource Planner and on procedures for confirming that resource constraints are represented accurately before they influence collaborative decisions.
S870: The Slot Coordinator shall receive training on the Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and applicable Business Rules Registry entries so that slot actions are applied consistently and transparently.
S871: The Network Operations Liaison and Airspace Sector Planner shall be trained to coordinate regional constraints, sector load conditions, and network measures using the Sector Load Monitor and Common Situation Display.
S872: The Airport Duty Manager shall be trained to recognize when an Airport Capacity Plan requires revision and when the operational state should move from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.
S873: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall be trained to explain weather uncertainty in operational terms and to verify that the Weather Ingest Gateway supports the assumptions used during briefings.
S874: The Emergency Response Coordinator shall participate in recurrent training so that emergency priorities are integrated into flow management decisions without obscuring command authority or safety responsibilities.
S875: The Deicing Coordinator shall receive seasonal refresher training on how deicing capacity assumptions are represented in demand and departure metering tools.
S876: The Data Governance Steward shall train operational users on data quality responsibilities, privacy expectations, and the correct interpretation of audit records in the Audit Event Ledger.
S877: The System Support Engineer shall train superusers on service status checks, access fault escalation, and safe use of the Contingency Operations Console during partial outages.
S878: Initial training shall include classroom instruction, supervised workstation practice, scenario walkthroughs in the Digital Briefing Room, and observed operational shadowing before independent system use is authorized.
S879: Recurrent training shall be required at least annually and after major changes to the Regional Flow Platform, Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, or Flight Data Exchange.
S880: Simulation exercises shall use realistic traffic samples, weather constraints, surface congestion, airline schedule pressure, handling resource shortages, and recovery objectives to test coordinated decision making.
